mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals a consumption contraction with offsetting housing demand, resulting in flat to mildly positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a paradoxical labor market where job creation is insufficient to absorb new entrants, leading to increased uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in CPIAUCSL above 4% while FEDFUNDS remains below 2% signals a surprise inflation surge with accommodative policy, which erodes real yields and supports S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% AND FEDFUNDS < 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 6-month moving average for five consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.4 percentage points for three consecutive months, regardless of GDP growth, signals persistent labor market softness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.
